HD.rationale: HD is a high-quality franchise in a cyclical trough — category-leading scale, ~17% market share, Pro pivot via SRS acquisition, and strong cash generation (Q1 OCF $6.03B, +39.5% YoY). However, the near-term fundamental picture is deteriorating: EPS declined -4.3% YoY on GAAP basis ($3.30 vs $3.45) despite +4.8% revenue growth, with gross margin compressing to 33.0% from 33.8% and operating margin to 11.9% from 12.9%. The PE at 22.0x is at the floor of its 365-day range (20.3x–28.8x), but this low multiple correctly reflects declining earnings power — the earnings yield of 4.5% barely exceeds the 10-year Treasury at 4.47%, offering near-zero equity risk premium. Balance sheet leverage remains aggressive at 6.78x liabilities-to-equity. The housing cycle is stalled (existing-home sales historically weak, mortgage rates >6.75%), and guidance embeds only 0%–2% comp sales growth. The structural franchise quality and Pro diversification support a mild positive tilt, but margin compression with no visible inflection, near-zero ERP, and speculative housing recovery timing cap the score well below +0.2. No credible near-term fundamental catalyst exists to trigger re-rating — buybacks are paused until H1 2027, and the Q1 beat was marginal ($0.02).
key_factors: Q1 FY2026 GAAP EPS diluted $3.30, down -4.3% YoY from $3.45 despite revenue growth of +4.8% YoY to $41.77B — margin compression is the driver
Gross margin compressed to 33.0% (Q1 FY2026) from 33.8% (Q1 FY2025); operating margin contracted to 11.9% from 12.9% YoY — cost-of-revenue grew +6.0% vs revenue +4.8%
PE diluted at 22.0x (2026-06-04), at the floor of its 365-day range (20.3x–28.8x) — multiple compression tracks earnings deceleration, not a mispricing
Earnings yield 4.5% vs 10-year Treasury 4.47% — near-zero equity risk premium leaves no valuation cushion
Operating cash flow $6.03B in Q1, +39.5% YoY — strong but likely reflects working-capital timing rather than operating leverage, since operating income fell -2.9% YoY
Total liabilities $94.03B vs equity $13.87B, liabilities/equity 6.78x — aggressive leverage with limited macro shock buffer
Housing market stalled: existing-home sales historically weak, mortgage rates above 6.75%, new-home sales near 2019 levels per 2026-06-03 reporting
FY2026 guidance: comp sales 0%–2%, EPS $14.69–$15.28, operating margin ~12.4%–12.6% — modest expectations with RBC flagging risk of miss
Pro customer pivot (~50% of sales) and SRS Distribution acquisition ($18.25B, June 2024) are credible long-term structural positives but depress near-term ROIC (25.4% from 31.3%)
Share repurchases paused since March 2024, resumption projected H1 2027 — no near-term buyback support for EPS
Lowe's trades at 17x forward P/E with 9% expected earnings growth vs HD's 20.7x and 5% — competitive valuation pressure
Price at $309.95 (2026-06-04), near 365-day low ($289.10), down -27% from peak $426.75 — price has correctly discounted fundamentals

sources_cited.excerpt: DGS10=4.47%, earnings_yield=4.5% — near-zero equity risk premium

Home Depot ended fiscal year 2025 with $164.7 billion in revenue — a 3.2% gain driven partly by its $18.25 billion acquisition of SRS Distribution — and held roughly 17% of the U.S. home improvement market; Pro Customer Revenue Share: ~50% of total sales
management anticipates resuming share repurchases once the company achieves an excess cash position, projected for the first half of 2027
RBC Capital lowered its price target to $340, citing stalled housing turnover and a worsened demand outlook
new-home sales near 2019 levels and existing-home sales historically weak; mortgage rates above 6.75%

Home Depot offers a higher dividend yield (2.97% vs 2.26%), Lowe's appears more attractive based on its lower valuation (Forward P/E of 17x vs 20.7x) and higher expected earnings growth (9% vs 5% annually)
Home Depot's Return on Invested Capital (25.7%) is slightly lower than Lowe's (26.1%)
